newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT HITS FRESH INTRA-DAY LOW ON IRAQI OIL.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT HITS FRESH INTRA-DAY LOW ON IRAQI OIL.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures hit fresh intra-day lows on Thursday as the expected resumption of Iraqi oil continued to pressure oil markets
September Brent was down 24 cents at $18.96 a barrel at 1123 GMT having earlier dipped to $18.97 after breaking technical support at $19.10.

Oil companies were jostling for position in the tanker market after Wednesday's news that United Nations oil experts or overseers had approved Iraq's pricing formula for it's oil. The pricing formula was passed to the U.N. sanctions committee which has until 1500 GMT Friday to raise any objections.
Otherwise the formula is accepted and Iraq can sell oil.
Adding downward pressure to the market is the sluggish Brent cargo market which is finding little support from the United States despite good refinery margins on both sides of the Atlantic.
Brokers see the next downside target on Brent around $18.90 an area heavily traded about a week ago.
IPE gas oil was down $2.50 a tonne at $172.75 at 1106 GMT having earlier punctured support at $173.50.
Brokers pegged next support at $171.25 while physical dealers said demand into Germany remains poor.
"There is some downward pressure on the physical market," said Leslie Nicholas of brokers GNI on London.
"But it was strange that the Venezuelan news didn't more of an impact" he added referring to Wednesday's news of force majuere on 2 or 3 gasoline cargoes at the Cardon refinery in that country.
